proposals.title: Self-made input: the network makes its own inputs by lowering its own training loss on targets it draws itself (starts from the same pink noise)
proposals.idea: Today the floor feeds pink noise. The network sees all noise images as about the same thing, so its deep layers stay quiet (F2: layer4 variance is .12-.25 of the stored answer). Training put the real data where the network's own loss is low and its outputs are sure and different from each other. So we let the network make its own input: start at the same pink noise and take a few gradient steps that lower the network's own training loss on targets the network draws itself, under random shifts, flips and zooms. For a language model this is plain sampling from the model itself, with no gradient. Only the input changes. The floor's Minitron ranking stays exactly as it is.
proposals.derived_from: F2 (check_bn.json): the scale is right at bn1 (ratio .93) and falls with depth (layer3 .26-.27, layer4 .12-.25). Means already rank at .78. So the input is wrong in the DEEP layers, and the fix must drive the input from the output side. F3 and the board row "Minitron on photos" (1.113 / 8.408 / 7.541) set the bar for this part. THEORY section 3: a threshold needs to know where inputs sit, and "whether the weights alone hold enough about the training inputs to set the scale is the next test". This proposal is that test. Essay line 111: transformation robustness is what made optimized images come out crisp ("same neurons, better microscope"). Essay lines 91, 113 and 569-573: free optimization reward-hacks in late layers, and a start near natural routes avoids the basin. Here the start is natural-spectrum pink noise, the steps are few, and each image gets its own target. Essay 287 and 701: a network trained on pure noise still borrowed textures, so noise sits far from the operating point. Prior art for language models (Williams et al. 2410.17170): the model's own samples serve as calibration data. Objects (picked by): ResNet-18 = per-channel input variance at all 20 BatchNorm layers (picked by check_bn.py, all layers). CLIP = every stream dim, head and MLP neuron that noisecut scores (picked by noisecut's own score sets, all units).
proposals.math:
Input in Fourier form, the same as pink:
  x(z) = chan_norm( irfft2( A * z ) ),  A = 1/f (A[0,0] = 0),  z0 = rfft2(w_seed)  ->  x(z0) = generic.pink(seed) exactly.
  chan_norm = mean 0, std 1 per image per channel (as pink), so no gain can come from louder pixels.
Each step k = 1..K, with a random transform t (roll by up to 16 px, flip with p .5, scale .9-1.1 then crop back to 224):
  ResNet (classifier): L = mean_i CE( f(t(x_i)), y_i ),  y_i ~ softmax(fc.bias), drawn once per image (the network's own class prior, about uniform).
  CLIP (contrastive tower): e_i = normalize(forward(T, t(x_i))),  e'_j = the previous step's embeddings (detached; at k = 1, a second view)
                            L = mean_i -log softmax_j( 100 * e_i . e'_j )_i      (100 = CLIP's own stored logit scale; each image is its own caption)
  z <- Adam(z, lr .05) on L.
K = 32. All knobs are fixed now and NEVER tuned on check_bn. Then noisecut runs unchanged on x(z_K).
Language model: x = sequences sampled from the model from BOS (temperature 1). Each token is a target the model draws itself, so no gradient is needed.
proposals.rule_transformer:
1. Add selfmade_vit(T, n=64, seed=1, K=32) in generic.py (or rules/selfcut.py). For each batch of 32, use the same seed as noisecut (seed*100000 + a). Keep w, z0 = rfft2(w), and A = 1/f as in pink().
2. Make z a leaf tensor that needs a gradient. Freeze all weights (requires_grad False) and run under torch.enable_grad(). Do the forward with vitgen.forward(Td, t(x(z))) on MPS.
3. Loss = self-InfoNCE at scale 100 against the previous step's detached embeddings (see math). Use Adam with lr .05 for 32 steps. After each step, x = chan_norm(irfft2(A*z)).
4. Save x_K as half to fanout/cache/self_clip_n64_k32_s1.pt. Load it if it exists.
5. Copy noisecut.py to rules/selfcut.py. In vit_scores, take x from the cache in place of generic.pink. Change nothing else.
6. Known-answer row: run with K = 0 (n = 64). It must equal noisecut computed on the first 64 pink images.
7. CLIP check (CLIP stores no answer): check_clip_stats.py. Compute the three noisecut score sets on 1,000 held photos (reading only). Report the Spearman rank correlation with the scores on pink and on selfmade, per block and as a median. Also report the RMS ratio of the loud dims (163, 419, 171, 573, 97).
proposals.rule_resnet:
1. Add selfmade_r18(A, n=256, seed=1, K=32). Use z0 from the same pink seed as noisecut (generic.pink(256, seed=1)), so K = 0 gives the floor input exactly.
2. Keep A in eval mode. The BN-folded inference map is allowed. No term looks at running_mean or running_var.
3. Draw y_i ~ softmax(A.fc.bias) with a fixed generator, once per image. Loss = CE(A(t(x)), y). Use batch 64, Adam with lr .05, K = 32, and the same transform t as for CLIP.
4. Cache x_K to fanout/cache/self_r18_n256_k32_s1.pt.
5. In rules/selfcut.py, r18() calls wide18.channel_scores(A, x_K) and then cut_from_a. Change nothing else.
6. In check_bn.py, add the keys "selfmade", "selfmade K=0" (must equal the pink row), "null: shuffled", and "plant: photo start".
7. Board: selfcut at f = .95, .5, .05 (ResNet) and f = .95, .5, .25, .05 (CLIP).
proposals.language_model: The rule is "the input is what the network makes when it lowers its own training loss on targets it draws itself". For a language model this is exact and needs no gradient: sample N = 128 sequences of 512 tokens from BOS at temperature 1, and feed them to the same Minitron ranking. The adapter is only the loss head: a classifier uses CE to a class drawn from its own bias, a contrastive tower uses self-InfoNCE at its stored scale, and a language model uses next-token sampling. A language model has no BatchNorm. So its check is the same as CLIP's: rank agreement of unit scores with real text, as a reading only. Published work (self-calibration) already shows this works for unstructured pruning and quantization, so P0 carries over with the least risk of any part.
proposals.photo_use: None in the calculation. The input comes only from the weights plus a pink-noise seed. Photos are read in four places, all as checks or scores: (1) the photo ceiling row of check_bn (1,000 held photos), (2) the CLIP known-answer check (1,000 held photos, reading only), (3) the planted fixed-point start (256 held ResNet photos, 64 held CLIP photos, reading only, never cached for a rule), (4) board scoring (1,000 test photos). BatchNorm running stats are the known answer of the check only. No loss term uses them.
proposals.prediction:
Written before any run.
Known-answer check (ResNet-18, check_bn), pink -> selfmade:
- Variance rank correlation median: .38 -> .60. Stages 1-2 rise less (.35 -> .45). Stages 3-4 rise most (.40 -> .65).
- Variance ratio median: .51 -> .90. Layer4 ratio: .12-.25 -> .5-1.5. A value above 2 means reward hacking.
- Mean rank correlation: .78 -> .85.
CLIP check (rank correlation with photo scores, median over blocks): pink about .5 -> selfmade about .7.
Board KL (1,000 test photos), floor -> selfcut:
- ResNet 95%: 1.760 -> 1.35 (photo row 1.113)
- ResNet 50%: 9.254 -> 8.8 (photo row 8.408, still at chance)
- ResNet 5%: 15.245 -> 10.0 (photo row 7.541)
- CLIP 95%: 1.139 -> 0.90
- CLIP 50%: 9.031 -> 8.5
- CLIP ViT-T shape: 10.404 -> 9.8 (target 1.801)
- CLIP 5%: 11.231 -> 10.8
Why: the ranking is still the floor's Minitron rule. Even real photos leave that rule at chance at 50% (8.408). So a perfect P0 cannot close F3 alone. The gain shows most at 5% (photos 7.5 against noise 15.2) and at 95%. The real value of P0 is that it puts P3 (where a gate opens) and P4 (the write) at the real operating point. Pass: variance rank median >= .55 AND ResNet 5% KL < 12. Fail: variance rank median < .45.
proposals.planted_test:
Two tests. Both must pass before the result is read.
(1) Fixed point. Start the SAME recipe (same K, lr, transform and target draw) from held photos, not pink: 256 for ResNet, 64 for CLIP, reading only. The real operating point is the known answer. A good generator must not move off it. Pass: check_bn variance rank median stays >= .90 (start .99), and the CLIP photo-score rank correlation stays >= .90. If it falls below .80, the recipe leaves the operating point, and its pink result means nothing.
(2) Exact floor. With K = 0 the recipe must give the floor numbers exactly (ResNet 1.760 / 9.254 / 15.245, and the check_bn pink row .38). For CLIP, K = 0 must equal noisecut on the same 64 pink images. This shows the change is only the K steps.
Calibration of the check, cheap and optional: mixes of 0/25/50/100% photos in pink must give a check score that rises with the mix.
proposals.null_test: Shuffled-weights generator. Run the same recipe with the same seeds and K, but make the images with a copy of the network whose weights are shuffled inside each conv or linear tensor (BN, LN and biases kept). Then check and score those images on the REAL network. Prediction: variance rank median stays near .38 (.30-.45), and the board KL stays within .3 of the floor at every size. If the null reaches the same gain, the gain comes from gradient energy plus the image prior, not from the trained network's own loss. A second, smaller null, only if time allows: the real body with a random head (fc, or CLIP proj, replaced by a Gaussian matrix of the same row norms).
proposals.prior_art:
- DeepInversion (Yin et al. 2020) and ZeroQ: they make images that match the stored BatchNorm mean and variance. That is not allowed here, and it works for BN networks only.
- DAFL (Chen et al. 2019): a generator with sure, balanced outputs. It is shown on small data sets.
- Plug-In Inversion (Ghiasi et al., ICML 2022, arXiv 2201.12961): it inverts ViTs and MLPs on ImageNet with augmentations only (centering, zoom, colour shift, ensembling) and no per-network regularizer. It uses class targets and judges images by eye. It does not use them as calibration input for a width cut.
- Self-calibration (Williams, Chrysostomou, Aletras, NAACL 2025, arXiv 2410.17170): a language model's own samples serve as calibration data for quantization and pruning. They match real data and sometimes beat it. Follow-ups (SGS 2025, IGSP 2606.03328) filter the samples.
Where published work stops: none of it makes a calibration input for a CLIP vision tower with no text targets. None of it scores a self-made input against BatchNorm stats while keeping those stats out of the objective. None of it tests a structured whole-network width cut at 50% and 5% with no training. That is the bar to pass.
proposals.risks:
1. Reward hacking (essay 91, 113, 569-573). Deep channels on easy routes get too loud, and the ranking leans toward channels aligned with the head. Sign: layer4 ratio > 2, or a stage-4 rank lower than stage 3. Built-in guards: transformation robustness, a pink start and only 32 steps.
2. Colour. Pink has independent colour channels (bn1 rank .65). The steps may or may not add the colour correlation photos have. The bn1 row of the check shows it.
3. CLIP self-InfoNCE may separate images only through the loud stream dims (F1), and leave heads and MLP neurons at noise level. The per-part rows of the CLIP check show it.
4. The CLIP sample shrinks from 256 to 64 images to fit the time. The K = 0 n = 64 row controls for this.
5. 256 ResNet targets cover only 256 of 1,000 classes. Run seed 2 and report the spread.
6. The time figures are estimates (forward speed from FANOUT.md times 3).
7. Even a perfect input leaves the floor rule at chance at 50%. P0 is the base for P3 and P4, not the fix for F3 by itself.
proposals.compute:
One torch job at a time on Mac MPS. The input is made once per network and cached. Every rule after that runs in seconds, as now. Estimates come from the FANOUT.md forward speeds (CLIP 14 s per 1,000, ResNet 3 s per 1,000), times 3 for the backward pass.
- ResNet: 256 images x 32 steps, batch 64. About 10 ms per image-step, so about 80 s. About 2 GB.
- CLIP: 64 images x 32 steps, batch 32. About 40 ms per image-step, so about 90 s. About 4 GB.
- Checks: check_bn about 30 s. CLIP check about 30 s.
- Plant and null: each costs the same as one generation.
- Board rows: about 1 min per network.
Whole round: about 10-12 min of torch, run one job after another. No GPU job.

proposals.title: p5rank: remove the unit whose loss moves the output least (written value x read gradient, per sample), weakest first, measured again after each step
proposals.idea: A unit matters only through what reads it, and the reading goes on to the final output. The written strength is the unit's own value on each token. The read strength is how much the final output moves when that value moves. The score is the product of the two, summed over tokens, then squared per input, then averaged. The rule removes the weakest units first in fixed steps and measures the network again after each step. So one nested order gives every size. The build is still a plain cut (no weight changes), so this change fixes WHICH units stay, not how they are repaired.
proposals.derived_from: THEORY section 1, row "Order of cutting" (written x read, weakest first, one ranking). THEORY section 2, Hamadouche & Hussain row (balanced Gramians from activations and output Jacobians). BOARD F1: the loud stream dims are the weakest by weight, so activity must be part of the score, and heads cost .758 of the 1.139 floor at 95%. CALC 2.4 and THEORY 7: the output reads only the class token, and block-12 patch firings are dead. Minitron averages over all 197 tokens, so it spends budget on units nobody reads. Essay 427: one large coordinate that no weight reads scales all other dims through LayerNorm, so its read strength sits in the norm. Essay "Toy Models": "a representation matters only through what reads it". Essay "Do Weak Activations Matter?": weak activations can be removed at almost no cost, and the strong ones carry the job. Squaring per sample weights strong firings. INDEX thread 1 and the board row "(check) Minitron on photos" 8.41 at ResNet 50%: a ranking alone cannot carry a cut job. This sets the upper limit of my prediction.
proposals.math:
Masks: one mask per unit per input sample, m[n,u] = 1 (kept) or 0 (removed). With binary masks the masked forward MUST equal the cut network exactly.
Probe (random direction on the output, equal weight, no class list):
  CLIP: o_n = 100 * e_n/||e_n|| (512-d output), r_n ~ N(0, I_512), J_n = r_n . o_n
  ResNet: z_n = logits, r_n ~ N(0, I - 11^T/1000) (centred), J_n = r_n . z_n
Per-sample unit gradient: G[n,u] = dJ_n/dm[n,u] = sum over tokens/positions t and channels c of a[n,u,t,c] * g[n,u,t,c]
  (a = written value, g = gradient of J_n at that value = read strength through everything downstream).
Score: S_u = (1/N) * sum_n G[n,u]^2.
Order of operations: multiply, sum over tokens, square per sample, then average. Do NOT square a gradient that is summed over the batch.
Meaning: E_r[G^2] = ||delta o_u||^2, the first-order output change when unit u is removed. This is the second-order KL if the class directions are spread evenly.
Greedy nested order: F = [1, .95, .85, .75, .65, .5, .4, .3, .25, .18, .12, .08, .05]. At each step, score the kept units on the masked network. In each set, set the masks of the lowest kept units to 0 until the set has the size of the next F (vitgen.sizes / wide18.widths). The removal order is the ranking. 95% contains 50%, 50% contains 25%, and 25% contains 5%.
proposals.rule_transformer:
New file rules/p5rank.py. Copy the noisecut pattern.
1. Write a masked forward of the vitgen dict. Each mask has a sample axis, shape (N, units), and requires grad.
2. Stream dim d: one mask m_s (N, 768), the same mask at every stream read: the input of ln1 and ln2 in all 12 blocks, and ln_post. Masked LN: mu = sum(m*x)/sum(m); var = sum(m*(x-mu)^2)/sum(m); y = m*((x-mu)/sqrt(var+eps)*g + b). With binary m this is vitgen's "ln" mode over the kept dims, so the gradient goes through mu and var. That is how the loud F1 dims get their read strength. Embedding writes (patch_w, cls, pos) and residual adds stay unmasked.
3. Head h of block i: a mask on its 64-d output, before o_w.
4. MLP neuron j of block i: a mask on the GELU output.
5. Input: generic.pink(128, seed 1), the same images at every step. Batch 16. Use one probe r per image (seeded). Read G from the mask gradients and add G^2 per unit.
6. Run the greedy schedule once. Save the kept index sets for every F to fanout/cache/p5rank_clip.pt.
7. vit(T, f): load the cache (build it if it is missing), then call vitgen.cut(T, stream, heads, mlp) with uniform widths.
8. Implementation check: on 16 pink images, the masked forward at the f = .5 masks against vitgen.cut at f = .5 must give KL < 1e-5.
9. Free extra row "p5rank1": the one-shot order from the step-1 scores only.
proposals.rule_resnet:
1. Use A.eval(). BN is a fixed affine map here (allowed: the folded inference map).
2. Inner channel of block (s,b): a mask (N, C) on relu(bn1(conv1(.))).
3. Stream channel of stage s: one mask m_s per sample, at every READ of that stream. The reads are: conv1 input of each block in stage s, conv1 AND downsample input of the first block of stage s+1, and the avgpool input for stage 4. The stem output is the stage-1 stream (cut_from_a uses st[0] for both). Leave the identity skip unmasked. The relu after the add acts per channel, so a channel that no reader sees has no effect. So binary masks equal cut_from_a exactly.
4. Probe: centred r_n ~ N(0, I - 11^T/1000) on the logits. Do NOT sample labels from the model's own softmax: on noise it puts weight on few classes.
5. Input: generic.pink(128, seed 1). Same greedy schedule. Save to fanout/cache/p5rank_r18.pt.
6. r18(A, f): build sc in the channel_scores format, with ranks from the removal order (later removal = higher score). Then call wide18.cut_from_a(A, f, sc) so the student class does not change.
7. Check: masked forward at the f = .5 masks against cut_from_a(.5) gives KL < 1e-5.
proposals.language_model:
Units:
1. A head, or a KV group in GQA: a mask on its output before o_proj.
2. A gated MLP neuron: a mask on SiLU(gate) * up.
3. A stream dim: one mask at the input of every RMSNorm and the final norm (masked RMSNorm, divisor sum(m)).
Point 3 is where the massive activations and attention-sink dims of language models get their read strength. This is the same effect as F1. The output is the model's own vocabulary logits. The probe is a centred Gaussian on the logits. When the input is at the model's operating point, the model's own Fisher can replace it (sample y from the model's p). Tokens: sum over positions, the same as patches. The generic input is the P0 question (for example, the model's own text sampled from BOS). Nothing in the rule depends on vision. Each architecture needs only a list of mask points.
proposals.photo_use: None in the ranking. The ranking uses weights plus generic.pink only. Photos are used for scoring only (board.py, 1,000 test photos). It does not use the CLIP class text: the probe is a random direction on the 512 output.
proposals.prediction:
Written before any run. KL on 1,000 test photos. Floor (noisecut) in brackets.
1. CLIP 95%: .55 [1.139]. Why: the read factor sees which heads feed the class token, and heads were .758 of the floor's cost.
2. CLIP 50%: 7.5 [9.031].
3. CLIP ViT-T shape (25%): 9.3 [10.404]. The trained target 1.801 stays far.
4. CLIP 5%: 10.8 [11.231], about no change.
5. ResNet 95%: .90 [1.760]. This beats photo Minitron 1.113 because the score is read-aware.
6. ResNet 50%: 7.8 [9.254]. Photo Minitron gets 8.41.
7. ResNet 5%: 7.5 [15.245]. Photo Minitron gets 7.54. The floor is confidently wrong. A read-aware order keeps the output-carrying channels.
Why the 50% and 25% gains are small: with a plain cut, every gate and write stays fixed. INDEX thread 1 and photo Minitron at 8.41 show that the best order alone cannot carry a cut job. The gap from about 7.5 to .856 and 1.801 is the next target for P3 (gate) and P4 (write).
Win rule: a gain counts only if it is larger than 2x the spread between pink seeds 1 and 2.
Free row p5rank1 (one shot): between noisecut and p5rank at 95%, and close to noisecut at 50%.
proposals.planted_test:
Each test is built so that the tool must see the effect. No photos are used to build them.
T1 CLIP, loud but unread. Object (picked by): the 30 block-6 MLP neurons with the highest noisecut score (picked by noisecut's own score). Plant: set pr_w[:, j] = 0 for these neurons. This gives the network T'. Pass: our S_j < 1e-10 x the median S of the block, all 30 removed at step 1, and noisecut keeps all 30 at 50%. Score both rules on T' (KL to T').
T2 ResNet, rescale with no change in function. Object (picked by): the 32 inner channels of layer3[0] ranked just above the 50% cut by our own step-1 score (picked by the rule itself). Plant: multiply the bn1 weight and bias of these channels by c = .01, and multiply their conv2 input weights by 1/c. ReLU is positive homogeneous, so the function stays the same (check KL(A', A) < 1e-6). Pass: our kept sets at 95/50/5 are identical with the same seeds, and the board KL changes by less than .01. Noisecut must drop all 32 channels (its score falls by 100x).
T3 CLIP, known answer. Object (picked by): stream dims 163, 419, 171, 573, 97 (picked by BOARD F1). Pass: all 5 are in the top 5% (top 38 of 768) of the step-1 stream scores. A weight-only score puts them near the bottom.
Implementation check: masked forward against the cut gives KL < 1e-5 (CLIP and ResNet, f = .5).
proposals.null_test: Named null "read-permuted". Use the same masks, input and greedy schedule. For each kept unit, compute the written part W_u = (1/N) sum_n sum_t ||a[n,u,t]||^2 and the read part R_u = (1/N) sum_n sum_t ||g[n,u,t]||^2. Then score with W_u * R_pi(u), where pi is a random permutation inside each set (fixed seed). This keeps the written strength and destroys the match between a unit and its own reader. p5rank must beat this null by more than 2x the seed spread. If it does not, the read factor does nothing. Input control (not a null on the rule): run p5rank with white noise in place of pink noise. If the two give the same KL, the input (P0, F2) limits the result, not the order.
proposals.prior_art:
Searched (one search, abstract and summary only, not read in full): Kwon et al. 2022, arXiv 2204.09656. It uses the Fisher information of head and filter masks on 1-2K task samples. It does a global mask search under a FLOPs limit, then a mask rearrangement and a layer-wise mask tuning. It does no retraining. BERT-base: up to 2.0x FLOPs reduction with less than 1% accuracy loss. It does not cut the stream (hidden) width. It needs task data and labels.
From memory, not read: Molchanov et al. 2019 (Taylor score (a*g)^2 on labelled data, then fine-tune). Theis et al. 2018 (Fisher pruning). LLM-Pruner 2023 (Taylor scores on groups, calibration text, then LoRA). SynFlow 2020 (data-free, weight path products, used for pruning at initialization, not for compressing a trained network).
THEORY 2: Hamadouche & Hussain use balanced Gramians only to pick widths per layer, then train. With no training they report MNIST 34.5%, CIFAR-10 11.4%.
Where they stop: every published removal score uses real samples, and none removes 50% of the stream in one shot with no repair. This proposal adds: a data-free input with an output probe in place of labels, stream dims scored through the norm, and one nested greedy order for all sizes.
proposals.risks:
1. Ranking alone cannot carry a cut job (INDEX thread 1, photo Minitron 8.41 at ResNet 50%). Expect most of the 50% gap to stay. That gap belongs to P3 and P4.
2. Input (F2): on pink noise, the ResNet stage-4 variance ratio is .12. ReLU gates open on different cells, so stage-4 read strengths may be wrong. The white-noise control and P0 address this.
3. First order: each step removes 5-15% of units. The sum of single-unit costs underestimates removing many units together. The greedy steps make this smaller but do not remove it.
4. The CLIP probe treats all 512 output directions as equal. It ignores the class-text geometry, which is not allowed in the calculation.
5. Sampling noise: N = 128 inputs with one probe each. Low-score MLP neurons can tie. Run seed 2 to get the spread.
6. Allocation: keep the board widths uniform (the ViT-T target is uniform, and wide18.Student fixes inner width = stage width). The ranking is in KL units, so it can also allocate widths. Next P5 row: pool heads and MLP neurons over all blocks per type, at the same total count, with at least 1 per block. vitgen.cut already takes lists per block. ResNet allocation needs a new student class, so it comes later. My lead: late CLIP blocks need fewer MLP neurons, because there only the class token is read.
proposals.compute: CLIP: 12 rescoring steps x 128 pink images, one forward and one backward each, batch 16, on MPS. About 4-6 s per step, so about 60-80 s once. The result is cached, so each board f only reads the cache. Peak memory about 3-4 GB at batch 16. If a step takes more than 10 s, use N = 64. ResNet-18: about 10 s in total. One torch job at a time. The runner runs it.

proposals.part: P1 Tree + P2 Read + P3 Gate (MLP neurons in CLIP, inner channels in ResNet-18). The floor's ranking (P5), stream cut (P6) and head cut stay unchanged. Heads stay deleted this round.
proposals.title: OR-merge: a deleted unit joins its branch's kept unit, and the merged gate opens on the union of its members
proposals.idea: The floor deletes weak units. This change merges each deleted unit into a kept unit of the same branch instead. A branch is found in the weights. A unit goes to the stronger unit that takes the same votes from the same parent (rule R1). The merged unit's read is the sum of its members' reads. Each member is scaled to one noise standard deviation, so no loud member owns the sum (the CALC 3.5 error). The merged unit's threshold is set so that it fires as often as ANY member fires (an OR). It is not set at the sum of the member thresholds (an AND, the CALC 3.2-3.3 failure). Every unit points to a stronger unit, so one forest gives the 95, 50 and 5% cuts as nested cuts.
proposals.derived_from: THEORY section 1, rows "Its read and firing" and "Its gate and firing": fire on the UNION (an OR), not the shared direction (an AND). Essay 239-251: a small model keeps a coarse neuron, "one curves & loops neuron instead of ten curve detectors". Essay 31: trust each neuron's natural threshold. Here each member's own threshold (z_i > 0) defines the union. CALC 3.2/3.3: the shared direction collapses onto one member. CALC 3.5: the loudest member owns the union, so members are standardized. OC-reads-w: sibling reads are 93-98% private, so "the threshold must sit low enough to catch the whole branch". Thread 1 + thread 4 (OC-rw): with fixed gates a cut job is lost. One carrier with a moved gate (.56/.76) about ties 501 fixed-gate carriers (.70/.76). N11-rates: the coarse unit fires more broadly (.40 vs .17). CALC 3.3 (Shonu's idea): siblings take the same votes from the same parents. CALC 3.7 C1: children fire where the parent is on (nesting), so summing siblings adds the shared parent part coherently (it grows as n) and the private parts incoherently (they grow as sqrt n). The sum leans to the branch root by itself. FANOUT F1/F2: absolute noise levels are wrong, so the gate is set by a RELATIVE rule (rate matched to the members' union rate on the same noise pass).
proposals.math:
Layer with units i: z_i = r_i.x + b_i (BatchNorm folded into conv1 for ResNet), a_i = phi(z_i), out = sum_i u_i a_i.
One teacher pass on generic input G (P0, now pink noise). Use it for mu_i, sd_i of z_i (full input) and rho_p = RMS of the scalar on each upstream write column p.
TREE (weights + G, one forest per layer, the same for all sizes):
  vote v_i[p] = (r_i . w~_p) * rho_p / sd_i over every upstream write column p (w~ = column centred over dims when an LN follows).
  parent pi(i) = argmax_p v_i[p].
  Order the units by the floor's score. pointer h(j) = argmax over units k ranked ABOVE j with pi(k) = pi(j) of cos(v_j, v_k).
  If no stronger unit shares the parent: h(j) = argmax over stronger k of v_k[pi(j)] (the strongest reader of j's parent).
  At size f, a deleted unit climbs h until it reaches a kept unit k. This gives group M_k = {k} + its deleted descendants.
READ: z'_i = r'_i.x' + b_i, with r' = the read restricted to the kept stream inputs and x' = the teacher's stream as the student sees it (kept dims, the student's own norm). mu'_i, sd'_i on G.
  zhat_M = sum_{i in M} (z'_i - mu'_i)/sd'_i / S_M, where S_M = std of that sum on G.
GATE: p_U = P_G(max_{i in M} z_i > 0) (each member at its own natural threshold, full input).
  t_M = the (1 - p_U) quantile of zhat_M on G. z_M = sd_k * (zhat_M - t_M).
  So r_M = (sd_k/S_M) sum r'_i/sd'_i and b_M = sd_k [ sum (b_i - mu'_i)/sd'_i / S_M - t_M ].
WRITE (default, NOT my change, P4 owns it): u_M = sum_i c_i u_i, c_i = E_G[a_i a_M] / E_G[a_M^2].
Identity: M = {k} with the full stream gives z_M = z_k and c = 1. At f = 1 the rule is the teacher.
proposals.rule_transformer:
File: rules/ormerge.py, with vit(T, f). Copy the noisecut pattern.
1. Kept sets: call noisecut.vit_scores(T) and top(). Stream dims sd and heads come from the floor, with no change.
2. One teacher pass on generic.pink(64, seed 1), BS 32 (DEV mps). For each block, save 8,192 random tokens of the stream entering ln2 (s). Also save the full fc pre-activation z (8192 x 3072) and the GELU output a.
   Save the RMS of each upstream write scalar: the embedded stream dims after ln_pre (parent column = e_d), each attention output channel before o_w (768 per block, parent column = o_w[:, c]), and each GELU output (parent column = pr_w[:, j]).
3. Votes for block b: V = ((fc_w * ln2.g) @ Wc) * rho / sd[:, None]. Wc = all upstream columns, centred over dims, with at most 43.8k columns at block 11. Chunk over 512 children and keep only argmax pi(i), plus V restricted to the top-64 parents of each unit for the cos. Use the mlp score from vit_scores for the order. Build h(j) as in math.
4. For each f: climb h to make the groups. x' = layer_norm(s[:, sd], g = ln2.g[sd], b = ln2.b[sd]). z' = x' @ fc_w[:, sd].T + fc_b. Make the assignment matrix A (3072 x m_kept, rows one-hot). Zs = ((z' - mu')/sd') @ A gives S_M = Zs.std(0). The union is ((z > 0).float() @ A > 0).mean(0). Get t_M by torch.quantile per column. Write the new fc_w rows and fc_b. Get a_M = gelu(z_M) on the tokens. c_i = (a_i * a_M[group(i)]).mean / (a_M^2).mean. pr_w[:, M] = sum c_i pr_w[sd, i].
5. Start from vitgen.cut(T, sd, heads, mlp_kept). Then overwrite fc_w, fc_b and pr_w of each block with the merged values. Do not change the heads, the norms, pr_b or the stream.
6. Checks: (a) f = 1 gives KL < 1e-3 through board.py. (b) A group of one with the stream uncut returns the same fc row (max diff < 1e-4).
proposals.rule_resnet:
Same file, r18(A, f).
1. Kept sets: wide18.channel_scores(A, generic.pink(256, seed 1)). Then cut_from_a(A, f, sc) gives S and the kept index sets (stream st[s], inner inn[s][b]). The floor is unchanged.
2. For each of the 8 inner layers (stage s, block b), fold bn1 into conv1 (weight * gamma/sqrt(var+eps), bias beta - gamma*mean/sqrt(var+eps)). This folding uses the network's own inference map, as FANOUT rule 2 allows. No statistic is read from it.
   Run the teacher on the same noise. Save the block input h and z = folded conv1(h) at 16,384 random (image, position) samples. Also save the RMS of each block-input channel on the noise.
3. Units = the inner channels. Parents = the block-input stream channels c. Vote v_i[c] = (sum over 3x3 of the folded W[i, c]) * rms(h_c) / sd_i. Use the floor's inner score for the order. Build h(j) as in math.
4. For each f: groups. z' = conv1 with the kernel sliced to the kept input channels (prev stream set), on the teacher's h restricted to those channels. Then mu', sd', S_M, the union rate p_U from the full z, and t_M as in math.
   New student conv1 row for kept channel k = (sd_k/S_M) sum_i W'_i/sd'_i. Set student bn1 for that channel to weight 1, bias b_M, running_mean 0, running_var 1 - eps.
   Write: a = relu. c_i as in math. Student conv2[:, k] = sum c_i A.conv2.weight[st[s]][:, i] (each is a 3x3 kernel).
5. The stem, downsample, bn2 and fc stay as the floor made them.
6. Checks: f = 1 gives KL < 1e-3. A group of one with the stream uncut returns the same channel.
Run time: < 10 s.
proposals.language_model: The parts are the same: units with a gate (MLP neurons), parents = every column that writes into the residual stream (embedding dims, o_proj columns, earlier down_proj columns), RMSNorm in place of LN (no centring of the columns). SwiGLU: the gate row (silu) gets the OR rule (standardized summed read, threshold at the union rate). The up row is linear, so it is summed with the same per-member weights as the gate read. The down write uses the same projection c_i on a_i = silu(g_i)*up_i. The generic input is P0's input. For a language model the network can make its own input with no data set: text it samples from the start token. That input also answers F2 (the network's own operating point). Heads stay deleted, as here. The code for parents, the forest, the read and the gate does not depend on the architecture. Only the adapter changes (which matrix is the read, the write, the norm).
proposals.photo_use: None in the calculation. The only input is generic.pink (64 images for CLIP, 256 for ResNet), seed 1, the same input the floor uses. BatchNorm is folded as the network's own map. Its running statistics are never read as data. Photos are for scoring only (board.py, 1,000 test photos).

proposals.planted_test: Twin split, through board.py (whole network, KL). Build a wider teacher T+. In every MLP block (CLIP) and every inner layer (ResNet), pick a random 10% of units (seed 5). Split each one into two twins with the same read and half the write each. For ResNet, give one twin a read x2 (bias x2) and a write x1/4, which is exact under ReLU. This tests the standardization. Check that KL(T+, T) < 1e-4. Then force the kept set = the original units (the twins are deleted) and run the rule. Pass: the OR-merge returns KL < .01 to the teacher, and the forest sends at least 99% of the twins home to their own original. Plain deletion of the twins must give KL > .05. Otherwise the test cannot see the effect, and the cut must grow to 30% of the units. Second check, one block, for thinking only: plant 3 children of one real parent (shared parent column + private random reads, each firing 10% on the noise). The merged unit must fire on at least 80% of the noise tokens where any child fires. The AND variant (bias = sum of thresholds) must cover at most 30%.
proposals.null_test: Named null: RANDOM PARTNER. Use the same read, gate and write formulas and the same forest shape (each deleted unit points to a stronger unit). But each pointer goes to a uniformly random stronger unit in the same layer (seed 11). This keeps the broader gate and the kept output mass. Only the tree is removed. It is the CALC 3.4 lesson: breadth and mass alone can win. Predicted null: ResNet 50% 7.6, CLIP 95% 1.05. Pass rule for P1: R1 pointers beat the random partner by at least .3 at ResNet 50% and by at least .03 at CLIP 95%. Otherwise the tree adds nothing, and the gain belongs to the moment-keeping gate. Control (not the null): MEAN-ONLY. Delete as the floor does, and add the deleted units' noise mean write into the next bias. This separates "keep the mean" from "move the gate". Predicted: ResNet 50% 7.8, CLIP 95% 1.06.
proposals.prior_art: Model folding (2502.10216): k-means on look-alike [read|write] rows, mean read, summed write. Data-free variance repair (Fold-AR) rescales, but the gate stays the averaged member gate (AND-like). Partners are look-alikes, not a branch. No LLM result above 20% removed. Neuron Merging (Kim 2020, 2010.13160): the pruned neuron goes to its most cosine-similar kept neuron. Only the write is added. The kept neuron's read and gate never move, so the merge is exact only for a positive multiple. ResNet-34 at 30% removed: 37.4% vs 73.3% dense. ZipIt (Stoica 2023) and FLAP (bias compensation with a calibration mean) need data. SliceGPT and Minitron delete and do not merge. Where published work stops: partners are look-alikes, and the merged gate is a member's own gate or an average gate. None sets the merged unit's threshold so that it fires on the union of its members. None picks partners by a shared parent across all layers at once. The bar to pass is model folding's merge at the same widths with no training. I did not run a search this round.
proposals.risks:
1. Main risk (OC-when hand_b): moving a kept sibling's gate by hand made 2 of 3 pairs worse. The merge moves every kept unit that takes members, so its own job can dilute. A CLIP 95% result above 1.139 flags this.
2. F2: pink noise is not the operating point (ResNet stage-4 variance ratio .12). The gate is relative, so it is partly protected. But the union rate and the quantile still come from noise. A better P0 input plugs in with no code change.
3. Hubs: at 5% one kept unit can take hundreds of members. Its union rate goes near 1, so it becomes a nearly linear unit. This keeps the mass but loses the gating.
4. Open loop: all statistics come from the teacher's stream, not the student's stream that drifts in deep blocks.
5. CLIP 50% and below can stay at chance because the stream cut and the head cut dominate. The visibility rows show this. It is a P6/head target, not a fail of P1-P3.
6. CALC 3.3 M5: in blocks 7-10 the weight-only vote families differ from the photo families (.14-.29 overlap). The tree in those blocks can be off. The random-partner null measures this.
7. Essay 31 warns against standardizing neurons. Here only the read sum is standardized. Each member keeps its own natural threshold in the union count.
8. The write is the plain projection default (P4). A bad write can hide a good gate. The f = 1 identity and the twin test protect the mechanics only.
proposals.compute: Mac, MPS, one torch job. CLIP: the floor's scoring pass (6 s) + one teacher pass on 64 noise images (about 5 s) + votes over at most 43.8k upstream columns per block, chunked (about 1 s per block) + groups and quantiles per size (about 1 s per block). Total about 30-40 s for all four sizes. Peak memory about 1.5 GB (8,192 x 3,072 float32 per block, one block at a time, plus the vote chunks). ResNet: 256 noise images, 16,384 samples per inner layer, votes are 512 x 512 at most. Under 10 s. The twin test adds one T+ build (2x the time).

proposals.title: One stream basis with free read maps: keep what the readers and the norm read
proposals.idea: The stream has no fixed basis, so the cut there is a subspace and not a list of dims. ONE operation sets it: keep the k-dim subspace that keeps the most of what the stream's readers receive. The readers are the linear maps after each norm AND the norm's divisor, which reads the stream's length. Writers write into the kept subspace. Each reading site reads its best linear estimate of the full stream from that subspace. That estimate folds into weights the site already has, so it is free. The loud dims stay because the divisor reads them: dropping them makes each token's kept share of its length swing. This is the essay's "unread dimension that scales all the others through LayerNorm". On ResNet the ReLU after each skip add fixes the stream basis. So the same objective picks whole channels, and the same free fold repairs the readers.
proposals.derived_from: Essay 421 and 585: one loud, unread coordinate scales the read dims through LayerNorm ("work with the architecture"). Essay 431: the directions that neurons write to and read from are the stream's units, and you can follow them across layers. Essay 753: a rotated representation is trivial. THEORY s1, Stream row: the cut is a projection. P5: rank by written x read. F1: the loud dims are the weakest by weight but needed, and RMS on noise finds them (.263 at 95% stream-only, against 10.85 for the weight cut). CALC 2.2 and 2.4: the KD student uses ONE 192-dim stream that is a linear view of the teacher's (class-token R^2 .97 down to .63), and the best map shifts with depth. So give each reading site its own read map, but one stored basis. CALC s1 SliceGPT: centre the stream, fold the norm gains, then the network is exactly invariant to rotation. Its per-block bases need a map on each skip link. INDEX thread 1: only 7% of a dropped neuron set's variance is linear in the survivors. This caps the ResNet fold. Fit statement: C_l and the read estimate L_l are least-squares on generic-input statistics. Derived from: the read error of each site's reader under the projection, minimized in closed form.
proposals.math:
Exact rms form first. J = I - 11^T/D. Centre every writer with J. Fold each norm's gain g_l and bias b_l into its readers: W_l <- W_l diag(g_l), bias <- bias + W_l_orig b_l. Every norm becomes 'rms' with g = 1 and b = 0.
At reading site l, take x_hat = x/sqrt(|x|^2/D) on generic input. Then C_l = E[x_hat x_hat^T] (uncentred). G_l = W_l^T W_l / tr(W_l^T W_l C_l) (each site counts once).
Small stream: z = Q^T x, with Q orthonormal (D x k). Reader at site l: W_l L_l, where L_l = C_l Q (Q^T C_l Q)^-1. Divisor: D*rho_l, where rho_l = tr(Q^T C_l Q)/D.
Read error at site l = tr(G_l (C_l - C_l Q (Q^T C_l Q)^-1 Q^T C_l)) + divisor error, where divisor error ~ Var_tokens(kappa)/(4 rho_l^2) and kappa = |Q^T x_hat|^2/D (per token).
Pooled closed form: C = mean_l C_l and G = mean_l G_l. Take the eigenpairs (v_i, mu_i) of C^1/2 G C^1/2. Candidate i: u_i = normalize(C^-1/2 v_i) (reduced-rank optimum).
Score s_i = mu_i/sum(mu) + delta_i, where delta_i = mean_l Var_tok((u_i . x_hat_l)^2 / D)/4.
Sort by s_i. Q_k = QR of the first k candidates in that order. The basis is nested, so one ranking gives every size.
Privileged basis (an elementwise nonlinearity on the stream): Q is limited to coordinate axes. Greedy pivot: pick j = argmax (R G R)_jj / R_jj, then R <- R - R[:,j] R[j,:]/R_jj. Fold x_D ~ mu_D + M(x_K - mu_K), with M = Sigma_DK Sigma_KK^-1.
proposals.rule_transformer:
vitgen first: norm() accepts an optional matrix gain n['G'] (k x k): out = (x*rsqrt(sum x^2/D+eps)) @ G.T + b. forward() adds W.get('proj_b', 0). n_params counts G and proj_b.
1. Convert the teacher to rms form (exact). Writers o_w, o_b, pr_w, pr_b <- J*. ln_pre: its output map becomes the matrix gain G0 = J diag(g_pre) with bias J b_pre. The embedding space before ln_pre is its own space: centre patch_w, cls and pos with J. For ln1_i (q,k,v), ln2_i (fc) and ln_post (proj): fold the gains into the readers and the biases into q_b/k_b/v_b/fc_b. For ln_post, proj_b = b_post @ proj. Set all norms to mode 'rms', g = 1, b = 0, D = 768. KNOWN-ANSWER CHECK: KL to the teacher is about 0 at full width, and again with a random rotation R (writers R^T*, readers *R).
2. Statistics: generic.pink(256, seed 1), the floor's input, through the rms teacher. There are 25 stream sites: ln1 and ln2 of each block over all 197 tokens, and ln_post over the class token ONLY. Accumulate C_l (768 x 768) per site. Do the same for the embedding space: the centred pre-ln_pre tokens, with reader G0^T G0.
3. Build the G_l from the step-1 reader weights. Pool C and G. Add a ridge of 1e-6*tr(C)/768*I. Do the eig of C^1/2 G C^1/2 to get the candidates u_i. Make a second pass over the same noise to get delta_i. Sort by s_i. Q = QR of the ordered candidates. Do the same for the embedding space to get Q_e.
4. Size: k = the largest value <= round(f*768) for which n_params <= the floor's n_params at f. Payment for the k x k ln_pre gain: 2 stream dims at the ViT-T shape (192 -> 190). The builder computes it with n_params.
5. Build. patch_w, cls, pos <- Q_e^T*. ln_pre: G = Q^T G0 L_e, b = Q^T J b_pre, D = 768*rho_e. Stream writers: o_w, o_b, pr_w, pr_b <- Q^T*. Each reader at site l: W <- W L_l. Each norm: D = 768*rho_l. proj <- L_post^T proj. Heads and MLP neurons: the floor's noisecut index sets, unchanged.
6. Print rho_l for each site. Print the per-token kappa (1st, 50th and 99th percentile) on the noise. Print the rank and cos of the candidates nearest e_163, e_419, e_171, e_573 and e_97. Run stream-only rows too (heads and MLP at full width): the rule and the floor's coordinate cut, at each f.
proposals.rule_resnet:
The ReLU after each skip add fixes the basis, so Q is limited to channels (adapter flag: privileged=True). A 1x1 map on the skip path is NOT used: it would cost C^2 per stage, and it cannot rotate past the ReLU. The fold below adds 0 parameters.
1. Run pink(256, seed 1) through A (eval, BN-folded inference map). For each stage s, pool the stream points of s: the stem output (s=1 only) and the outputs of blocks (s,0) and (s,1). Get the channel mean mu and covariance Sigma over images x positions.
2. Readers of the stage-s set: conv1 of (s,1); conv1 AND downsample of (s+1,0); conv1 of (1,0) for s=1; fc for s=4. The identity skip copies the kept channels and has no fold. For each reader: W_eff = weight * bn.weight/sqrt(running_var+eps) per out channel (folded weights, not data). G = sum over out and taps of w w^T, divided by tr(G Sigma). G_s = the mean over the stage's readers.
3. Rank the channels by the greedy read-weighted pivot (math field). The order is the stream score (score = -rank). wide18.cut_from_a(A, f, dict(stream=..., inner=floor channel_scores['inner'])).
4. Fold into every reader of the set: M = Sigma_DK (Sigma_KK + 1e-3*mean diag*I)^-1. conv weight[:, K] += weight[:, D] contracted with M, per tap. Then bn.running_mean -= sum over taps of weight[:, D](mu_D - M mu_K). Work in the conv's own units, on the kept out rows. For fc: weight_K += weight_D M, and bias += weight_D(mu_D - M mu_K). The parameter count stays exactly the floor's.
proposals.language_model: A pre-norm LM is the simple case. RMSNorm needs no centring step. The embedding writes straight into the stream, so there is one space, no matrix gain and no dims to pay. Sites: the attention norm and the MLP norm of each layer, plus the final norm. Readers: q, k, v / gate, up / lm_head (gains folded). Writers: embed, o, down. One Q is stored. Each site's L_l folds into its own readers, so there are no skip maps and the count is legal. LMs also have a few loud coordinates that the norm reads. The divisor term keeps them with no coordinate rule, because the step is rotation-covariant. The generic input becomes random token sequences (P0 is still open). The class-token rule becomes 'final-norm site on the positions the loss reads'.
proposals.photo_use: None in the calculation. Only generic.pink(256, seed 1), the floor's own input. Weights include ResNet's BN-folded inference map. BN running_mean and running_var are never used as statistics. They are only edited as the target of the fold. Photos: scoring only, 1,000 test.
proposals.prediction:
Written before any run. Whole network, P6 changed only (heads, MLP and ResNet inner channels = floor):
CLIP 95%: .90 (floor 1.139). F1 bounds the gain: the stream costs .263 of the 1.139, and the rule keeps about .03 of that.
CLIP 50%: 8.3 (floor 9.03). CLIP ViT-T shape: 9.8 (floor 10.40). CLIP 5%: 11.0. These stay near chance because the floor's head and MLP cuts dominate. One head per block alone already costs .758.
Stream-only rows (heads and MLP at full width), rule vs floor coordinate cut: 95% .03 vs .263; 50% .6 vs about 4; 25% 2.5 vs about 7; 5% 8 vs about 10. Why: CALC 2.2 gives the teacher's top 192 directions .76-.96 of the stream variance (photos, all tokens). The read folds and the divisor fix remove the scale error. About 10-20% of the read energy is still lost per site, and it compounds over 25 sites.

proposals.planted_test:
CLIP, rotation: build the exact rms-form teacher with a random orthogonal R applied to the stream (writers R^T*, readers *R). Its KL to the teacher is about 0. The rule must give the same KL (within .01) on the teacher and on the rotated teacher at every f, because every step is coordinate-free: the basis, the folds, the divisor term and the ln_pre space. The floor's coordinate cut, stream-only at 95%, must fail on the rotated teacher. The loud energy spreads over all coordinates, so the RMS ranking no longer finds it. Expect KL well above .263.
ResNet, duplicate channel: widen stage 4 by one channel that copies channel c exactly. Copy c's writer rows (conv2 and BN of both blocks, downsample row) and split c's reader weights half and half. KL to A stays about 0. Then cut only the copy: the fold must give KL < .01, and the no-fold floor gives KL > 0.
proposals.null_test: N1, prior-art null (SliceGPT form): the same build with G = I and no divisor term. This is one global energy PCA with the same folds and rho. If it ties the rule stream-only at 25% (within .3 KL), the read weighting adds nothing. N2, weights-only null: C = I. Then the basis = the top eigvecs of G, L_l = Q, and there is no divisor term. Predicted chance at every f, as in F1, because it drops the loud dims. This shows that the generic input is what keeps them. Random-subspace null: a random Q with the same folds. Predicted chance at 50% and below.
proposals.prior_art: CALC s1 only (no search spent). SliceGPT: centres and folds the norms, then rotates each block into the PCA basis of that block's normed input. It uses 1,024 calibration sequences and a D x D map on each skip link. Llama-2 7B, mean zero-shot accuracy: 69.0 dense, 55.5 at 25% of the stream removed, 51.5 at 30%. Perplexity 5.47 -> 17.17 at 50%. No vision results. Model folding: k-means merges, up to 20% removed on LLMs. Minitron: activation ranking, then training. Published methods with no training stop at cuts of about 20-50%. This rule differs in four ways: one stored basis plus free per-site read maps (no skip maps, so the count is legal); a written x read basis in place of energy PCA; an explicit divisor term for the loud dims; and generic input in place of calibration data. The ResNet fold is close to Neuron Merging's compensation into the next layer (THEORY s2: per layer, cosine-matched), but here it is a least-squares estimate over the whole kept set.
proposals.risks: 1. Noise statistics: C_l and M are least-squares on pink noise, and F2 shows that noise is not the operating point (ResNet: rank corr .38, variance ratio .12 in stage 4). The fold can then point the wrong way. The ridge limits this, and N2 isolates it. 2. The divisor fix is per site, on average. The delta term keeps kappa nearly constant only to first order. Watch the printed kappa spread. 3. The ln_pre matrix gain costs k^2 (paid with 2 stream dims at ViT-T, about 6 at 95%). 4. C^-1/2 is ill-conditioned along weak directions. Use the ridge, and check that the candidates of the top ranks are well conditioned. 5. At 50% and below, the floor's head and MLP cuts hide the P6 gain in the whole-network KL. The stream-only rows are the honest readout, and the whole-network rows decide. 6. The q and k reads enter a softmax. A least-squares read estimate is a first-order proxy for them. 7. Pooling the sites into one C and G is an approximation. The per-site L_l takes up part of the depth shift (CALC 2.4).
proposals.compute: CLIP: 2 passes of the teacher on 256 pink images, at about 6 s each (the floor's statistics pass is 6.0 s on MPS). One eig of 768 x 768 plus the fold matmuls take under 1 s. Total about 15 s. Memory: 25 sites x (C_l + G_l) x 768^2 x 4 B, about 120 MB. ResNet: 1 pass of about 1 s, greedy pivots on matrices up to 512 x 512 and the folds take under 1 s. Total about 2 s. Builder time: about 1 h. The rms conversion (about 40 lines plus the KL-0 check) is the main part.

proposals.title: Reader-matched write: kept writes solved against the kept readers
proposals.idea: Each kept unit takes on the message of the cut units in its layer. It carries the share that it can predict from its own firing. The fold uses the kept units' firings on the generic input, with uncentered moments and no intercept, so a common scale error cancels. Each writer then writes onto the kept stream dims in the way the KEPT readers downstream read the stream. When a stream dim is cut, its content moves onto the kept dims that the kept readers read the same way. Both steps come from one closed-form solve of one error: the input error of each kept downstream reader, weighted by how much that reader moves the output. This changes only the write weights and write biases of kept units. Kept sets, reads, gates and norms stay exactly as noisecut makes them.
proposals.derived_from: THEORY section 1, P4 row: "the branch's message, as the COARSE readers downstream read it. New. Every past fold kept A's fine readers." Essay 469-471: parts are "built to be read ... by its downstream readers" and the goal is to "become another reader". Essay 699: "a representation matters only through what reads it". Essay 71: a signal "barely reaches the output" when its readers do little with it, so the downstream sensitivity sets the weight. VM8.3 P1: training made the stream error 21-41% LARGER and the KL lower, so the stream error is not the KL's target. VM8.2b: the gain of training on top of C is mostly a channel change of the kept writes, and A (below) is a channel map. OC-q-write: A's readers do not take the children's summed write as one message (reader energy outside the fold's message .71), so the message must be measured in reader space. VM3: an LS fold on photo firings recovers .71 with fixed gates, so the unit fold is real but needs a firing source. Here that source is the generic input, made scale-free for F2. VM8.3 P2: the pooled Fisher carried no information, and the algebra below shows why. F1 and F3 for the floor.
proposals.math:
Writer layer w. Big firings a(x) in R^n (kept units K, cut units C), big write W (D x n), bias c. Cut write W' (d_K x k), bias c'. Kept reader r has read row rt_r in R^D. rt_r is the effective read through its norm: LN, rt = (gain*r - mean(gain*r))/sigma_b. ResNet uses the raw conv tap row, with the gradient taken at the pre-BN output. Its K part is rt_{r,K}.
ERROR (minimized): L_w = E_x sum over kept readers r after w of g_r * ( rt_{r,K}^T (W' a_K + c') - rt_r^T (W a + c) )^2, with g_r = E_x (ds/du_r)^2.
s = v^T z_out, where v ~ N(0,I) is an isotropic probe on the output (CLIP: the normalized 512 embedding. ResNet: the centred logits). That is the KL Fisher at maximum uncertainty, and its scale cancels.
WHY THIS IS THE KL: KL ~ 1/2 dz^T F dz, with dz = sum_r J_r du_r. In the CUT network every path from a write to the output goes through a kept reader (the skip only carries the stream to later readers). Cut readers do not exist. A diagonal Gauss-Newton over reader inputs gives 1/2 sum_r g_r du_r^2 = L_w. The stream error |dx|^2 also counts directions that no kept reader reads.
SOLUTION (exact, because g_r does not depend on x): M = sum_r g_r rt_r rt_r^T (D x D, kept readers only). A = pinv(M_KK) M_KC. P = S_CK (S_KK + lam I)^-1, with S = E[a a^T] uncentered on the generic input. lam = tr(S_KK)/N_samples (Derived from: the sampling noise of S_KK at N samples).
W' = [I | A] (W_{:,K} + W_{:,C} P), c' = [I | A] c.
PLAIN STATEMENT: the reader weight cancels from P. "As the kept readers read it" acts only through A, the fold of the cut stream dims onto the kept dims under the kept readers' metric. In VECMATH the stream and the readers were never cut, so A = 0 there. That explains VM8.3 P2. Here A is the new term.
proposals.rule_transformer:
1. Kept sets: noisecut.vit_scores(T) and vitgen.sizes, giving sd, hk, mk. Start from W = vitgen.cut(T, ...). No change to reads or norms.
2. Noise pass (big T, generic.pink(128, seed 2), batch 32, no grad). Per block, accumulate the uncentered S_head = E[o o^T] (768 x 768, o = the concatenated head outputs before o_w) and S_mlp = E[gelu gelu^T] (3072 x 3072). Pool over all tokens. Move to float64 on the CPU.
3. Sensitivity pass (big T, pink(64, seed 3), with grad). Forward with retain_grad on the q, k, v and fc pre-activations of every block and on the 512 output. s = v^T normalize(e_cls), 4 probes v ~ N(0, I_512). g_r = mean over images, tokens and probes of (ds/du_r)^2. Record sigma_b = mean token RMS of (x - mean x) at each ln1, ln2 and ln_post input.
4. Read rows of the kept readers only: q/k/v rows of the kept heads (ln1_b), fc rows of the kept neurons (ln2_b), and the 512 proj columns (ln_post, class token). rho = gain*row, rt = (rho - mean(rho))/sigma. Add g_r rt rt^T to M.
5. Accumulate from the end. M = M_out. For b = 11 down to 0: M_mlp[b] = M, then add block b's fc readers, then M_attn[b] = M, then add block b's q/k/v readers. M_first = M after block 0.
6. For each position: A = pinv(M_KK, rcond 1e-6) M_KC (K = sd). F(x) = x_K + A x_C. rcond Derived from: the float64 noise floor.
7. MLP of block b (K = mk): P from S_mlp. pr_w' = F_mlp[b](pr_w[:,K] + pr_w[:,C] P), pr_b' = F_mlp[b] pr_b. Heads (K = the 64 rows of each kept head): P from S_head. o_w' = F_attn[b](o_w[:,K] + o_w[:,C] P), o_b' = F_attn[b] o_b.
8. ln_pre bias b'_K = F_first(b_pre), because it is a write. UNCHANGED: patch_w, cls, pos, the ln_pre gain, every ln gain and bias, q/k/v/fc reads and biases, ln_post, proj.
9. Return the dict.
proposals.rule_resnet:
1. Kept sets: wide18.channel_scores on pink(256, seed 1), then cut_from_a, giving S and kept. No change to reads.
2. Fold every BN of A into its conv (weight times gamma/sqrt(var+eps), bias beta - gamma*mu/sqrt(var+eps)). This is the allowed inference map. In S, write the folded convs and set each BN to identity (weight 1, bias = the new bias, mean 0, var 1-eps).
3. Noise pass (A, pink(128, seed 2), no grad). For each of the 8 inner spaces, S_inner = E[i i^T] over images and positions (i = ReLU(bn1(conv1)), uncentered).
4. Sensitivity pass (A, pink(64, seed 3)). Hooks with retain_grad on the pre-BN outputs of every conv1, every downsample conv and the fc logits. s = v^T(z - mean z), 4 probes v ~ N(0, I_1000). g_o = mean over images, positions and probes of (ds/du_o)^2.
5. M per writer position, from the kept readers' raw rows only. Add sum over o of g_o sum over the 9 taps of w_{o,:,t} w_{o,:,t}^T. Stage s stream readers: block1.conv1 of stage s (kept inner rows), stage s+1 block0 conv1 (kept inner) and downsample (kept st[s+1]), or the fc rows for s = 3. Positions: (a) stem, and also downsample + block0.conv2 for s >= 1: readers = everything after (for s = 0 also layer1.0.conv1). (b) block0.conv2: block1.conv1 + the next stage. (c) block1.conv2: the next stage or fc only.
6. A = pinv(M_KK, rcond 1e-6) M_KC (K = st[s]). F = [I | A].
7. Inner unit fold per block (K = inn[s][b]): P from S_inner, the same lam rule. For each tap t: W2'[:,:,t] = F(W2[:,K,t] + W2[:,C,t] P). Bias2' = F bias2. The same-position regression is exact per tap.
8. Downsample: rows F, bias F, input columns sliced (they are reads, so they stay). Stem conv1: rows F, bias F, pixel input unchanged.
9. UNCHANGED: conv1/bn1 reads, fc, avgpool, maxpool, the ReLU after the add.
proposals.language_model: The adapter is the same list of (writer matrix, firing tensor) and (reader rows, norm). Units are the SwiGLU neurons (firing = silu(gate)*up, write = a down_proj column) and the heads (an o_proj block). For GQA the shared k/v rows count as readers. The stream is the residual with RMSNorm, so rt = gain*row/sigma with no centring. Readers are the q/k/v/gate/up rows of the kept parts and the lm_head rows. The output probe is isotropic over the centred vocab logits, which is the KL Fisher at maximum uncertainty and needs no labels. The generic input is whatever P0 settles on (for example random token sequences or the model's own samples). The solve is the same closed form. M is d_model x d_model per layer position. S is d_ff x d_ff per layer, and it can be built in chunks. It needs no data set.
proposals.photo_use: None in the calculation: weights, pink noise seeds 1, 2, 3 and isotropic random probes only. No BatchNorm running statistics are used as data. They enter only through the allowed folded inference map, which the network itself runs. Photos are used for scoring only (the board's 1,000 test photos, KL and agree).
proposals.prediction:
Anchors: noisecut floor. Flat-output level = ln(1000) - H(teacher). CLIP: 6.28, measured now with numpy from clipkd/out/teacher_test.npz (5,000 photos 6.281, one per class 6.281). ResNet: about 5.7, an ESTIMATE from typical ResNet-18 entropy (about 1.2), not measured.
CLIP (floor 1.139 / 9.031 / 10.404 / 11.231):
- 95%: .80. Mainly the uncentered fold of the one cut head per block (F1: .758 alone) and of the MLP (.205).
- 50%: 7.0. Above flat, so the network is still confidently wrong.
- ViT-T 25%: 8.8. Above flat.
- 5%: 10.6. Above flat.
ResNet (floor 1.760 / 9.254 / 15.245):
- 95%: 1.05. Near photo-Minitron 1.11. VM3 recovered .71 on photos. Noise firings are expected to give about .4 of the cut damage.
- 50%: 6.2. Around flat, ABOVE the 5.7 estimate. The uncentered P carries the cut half's mean message into the fixed-gate readers, and that removes most of the confidently-wrong part.
- 5%: 9.0. Above flat. 26 kept channels can carry only the mean pattern of 486 cut ones.
Report agree next to every KL. Predicted agree gain over the floor: +10 points at 95% (both networks) and +5 points at 50%.
Why CLIP gains less than ResNet at 50% and below: an estimated LN scale error. noisecut uses LN over the kept dims. F1's printed RMS (dim 163 at 8-10 against a median of .1-.3) suggests that the loud dims hold most of the token norm. So the cut stream's sigma is about 1.35x the big one at 50% and about 1.8x at 25% (ESTIMATE, not measured). That error shrinks every kept read, and no write can fix it, because LN does not change when x is scaled. The gap to the KD student (1.801) is predicted to stay large. It belongs to P3 (gates), P6 (norm scale) and the ranking.
proposals.planted_test:
Function-preserving splits. The big network stays exact: check this with the identity rule, which must give KL 0.
(a) Units, both networks, at f = .95. In every block, pick 32 MLP neurons (CLIP) or 32 inner channels (ResNet) that noisecut keeps. Append an exact copy of each (same read row, same bias, same BN). Split the write 50/50 between the original and the copy. Force the copies into the cut set. The floor then loses half of each of those 32 writes. The rule must find P[copy, original] = 1, because the firings are identical on any input. Pass: (KL_rule_planted - KL_rule) <= .05 x (KL_floor_planted - KL_floor), and (KL_floor_planted - KL_floor) >= .05, so the board can see the effect.
(b) Stream, ResNet stage 3. Duplicate 16 kept stream channels. Halve every writer row into the two copies (stem/downsample/conv2 folded, so ReLU(z/2) + ReLU(z/2) = ReLU(z)). Give both copies the original read column in every reader. Cut the copies. The M columns of each copy then equal its original's, so A must map copy to original with weight 1. Pass: the same 5% bar.
Object (picked by): the kept writes of kept units, kept readers and cut sets, all picked by noisecut's ranking. The planted copies are picked by the builder at random among the kept units (seed 0). No R1 children are used. P is a same-layer firing regression, and the cut units are not called siblings or children.
proposals.null_test:
Named null: BROKEN PAIRING, with matched norm. Use the same rule, the same code and the same moments, but break the pairing:
- P_null = the P computed from firings with the kept and cut samples taken from DIFFERENT noise images (shuffled pairing). In expectation this keeps only the product of the means, so the mean message and the norm are matched.
- A_null = A with its columns permuted at random among the cut dims (same norm, wrong dim).
Pass bar: the rule beats the null by >= .5 KL at 50% on both networks, with higher agree.
Reader-part check (the claim "as the KEPT readers read it"): the same rule with M = I over A's full stream, which is the stream-matching target. Then A = 0 and only the unit fold stays. Pass bar: the rule is better by >= .3 at 50% and 25% on CLIP and at 50% on ResNet. If this fails, A adds nothing, and the reader metric is not the right target at the whole-network level.
Floor = noisecut itself.
proposals.prior_art:
Read, per THEORY 2 and CALC 1:
- Neuron Merging (2010.13160) adds a cut neuron's write to its most cosine-similar kept neuron. It works per layer, from weights only, and its target is the next layer's input. ResNet-34 at 30% removed: 37.4% against 73.3%.
- Model folding (2502.10216) uses the sum write per k-means cluster and a variance repair with no data. LLM work stops at 20% removed.
- SliceGPT uses a PCA stream projection with calibration text, 25-30% removed.
- Minitron trims and then distills.
From memory, NOT read in this round: OBS/OBC/SparseGPT/ZipLM and FLAP. They compensate against the layer's own output (the full next-layer input) with calibration data. DFQ bias correction (Nagel 2019) needs BatchNorm statistics, which are banned here. LLM Surgeon uses KFAC of the loss Fisher with data.
Where published work stops: compensation targets the full layer output, or the full stream, with data or BN statistics. No method found here solves a write against the KEPT readers of the residual stream across all later blocks, with the stream and the readers cut together, from weights plus a generic input, at 50% or more removed. That last combination is the bar to pass. It is not a ceiling.
proposals.risks:
1. CONFOUND, CLIP: the LN scale. noisecut's LN over the kept dims divides by a sigma that is an estimated 1.35x (50%) to 1.8x (25%) the big one. That figure is inferred from F1's printed RMS, not measured. The cause is that the loud, weakly read dims stay. A also adds energy to the kept dims, which can make this worse. Cheapest control: print sigma'_b/sigma_b on noise for the floor and for the rule (one forward). Also score the rule once with vitgen norm mode "rms" and D = 768 as a P6 control. The P6 theorist owns that change.
2. F2 exposure. P is a regression ratio with no intercept and uncentered moments, so a common scale error per layer cancels. The per-channel pattern does not cancel (rank correlation .38 on noise). g_r enters A only as ratios between readers, but gate slopes on noise are off the operating point. The planted test cannot catch this. Only the null and the board can.
3. LS shrinks the predicted message, so the kept readers' input variance falls. Fixed gates and fixed BN then sit at the wrong quantile. That belongs to P3 (threshold). The rule does not fix it, and at 50% and 5% it may cap the gain near the flat level.
4. An input-independent g_r. VM8.3 shows that per-photo gating carried most of training's gain at large cuts (q explained only .32 and .23 at cuts 192 and 384). A per-input weight does not factor and is not in this rule.
5. Writers are solved one at a time, so cross-writer cancellation in the stream (for example big offsets that cancel) is ignored.
6. ResNet: the ReLU after the add makes the stream fold approximate where the folded sign changes. Zero padding makes the per-tap fold inexact at borders.
7. noisecut's ranking error (ResNet 95%: 1.76 against 1.11 with photos) limits every write rule.
proposals.compute:
Mac, MPS, one torch job.
ResNet: noise pass with 128 images about 3 s, backward with 64 images and 4 probes about 5 s, folds under 2 s. About 15 s in all, under 1 GB.
CLIP: noise pass with 128 images about 30 s (12 x 3072^2 float32 moments = 450 MB, or block by block), backward with 64 images and 4 probes about 30-40 s, 12 pinv/solves of at most 3072^2 about 5 s. About 1.5 min, under 3 GB. One run gives all sizes (the moments and g are computed once and reused for 95/50/25/5).
Builder time: about 1-1.5 h for both adapters. The backward pass with retain_grad is the largest part.

problems: CLIP uses n = 64 images. The floor uses 256. So the board row changes two things: the input and the sample size. A comparison with the floor (1.139 / 9.031 / 10.404 / 11.231) does not isolate the input.

The CLIP loss is not CLIP's training loss. CLIP trains image against text, and text is banned. Self-InfoNCE against the previous step's own embeddings is a SimCLR-type proxy. The text says 'lowers its own training loss', and for CLIP that is not true.
The ResNet 'own targets' are draws from softmax(fc.bias), which is close to uniform. So in practice the rule is 'make the network sure of a random class'. That is fine, but say it plainly.

Planted test (1), the photo start, probably passes with no real test. 32 Adam steps from a photo make a small adversarial change. Batch statistics stay photo-like whether or not the recipe is good. The test cannot show that the check sees the effect.
The photo-mix calibration (0/25/50/100% photos) is the only test that shows check_bn can see a better input. The proposal calls it optional.
Knobs (K, lr, transforms) are fixed now. That is correct. But if the run fails, a retune on check_bn would use BatchNorm statistics as data. That is a rule break.
The CLIP check's pink baseline (about .5) is not measured.
The time figures are estimates (forward speed times 3). They are plausible: about 80-90 s per network.
fixes: Compare the CLIP board rows with the K = 0, n = 64 row, not with the floor. Or run CLIP at n = 256 (about 6 min, still inside the budget).
Add a 'Derived from:' line for the CLIP proxy: a contrastive tower with no text, so each image is its own caption, at the stored scale 100. Do not call it CLIP's training loss.
Make the photo-mix calibration mandatory. Keep the photo-start test as a guard only. It does not count as the planted test.
Write the rule into the proposal: no knob is tuned on check_bn. Any tuning uses only the held-split KL (board --split held).
Measure the pink row of the CLIP check before the selfmade run.
Keep the shuffled-weights null. It is a real null, and chan_norm blocks gain from louder pixels.
Report agree next to KL. Also report the flat-output level (see notes).
verdicts.generic: Yes, with the most support of the five. For a language model the rule becomes sampling from the model itself (Williams et al. self-calibration). The gradient recipe is only the vision adapter. The augmentations have no language-model analogue, but the language model does not need them.

verdicts.part: P1 Tree + P2 Read + P3 Gate (OR-merge)
problems: It changes more than one part: tree, read and gate together. It also changes the write. The floor deletes a unit. This rule projects the deleted writes into the kept unit (u_M = sum c_i u_i). That is a P4 change, and the proposal calls it 'the default'. It is stacked methods under the one-part rule.

A group of ONE also changes. With the stream cut, every kept unit is re-centred, re-scaled to sd_k and re-thresholded to its noise firing rate. So part of any gain can come from this moment repair, with no merge at all. The ResNet prediction itself counts on this ('re-centres each inner unit'). No row isolates it.
The core P3 claim (OR beats AND) is tested only in one block 'for thinking only'. No whole-network row compares the OR threshold with an AND threshold. The rules say a one-block check never decides.

R1 says 'readers of the parent's write, in weights'. The vote multiplies by rho_p, the RMS of the parent on noise, and divides by sd_i on noise. That is weights plus generic input. It is an extension of R1, not R1.

Mechanics bug: torch.quantile refuses inputs above 2^24 elements (about 16.8M). 8,192 tokens x about 2,918 kept neurons at CLIP 95% is about 23.9M elements. The call will fail. It also may not run on MPS.
The twin planted test recovers identical twins (cos 1, same parent). That is a mechanics check only. It does not show that the OR gate helps on real branches.
SwiGLU in the language-model text is approximate. A sum of gate*up products is not the product of the summed gate and the summed up. The 'firing' definition (silu(g) > 0) ignores the sign of up.
The build is well over one hour: forest, votes over up to 43.8k columns per block, groups, quantiles, writes, two adapters, a T+ build, a random-partner null, a mean-only control and visibility rows.
The predictions depend on the 50% split by part. That split is not measured (the proposal says so).
The planted tests do not name 'Object (picked by)' in the required column form.
fixes: Hold the write fixed across all ablation rows, so the write cancels in the comparison. Then report these rows at whole-network KL: (a) floor; (b) singleton re-standardization only, no merge; (c) R1 groups with an AND gate (threshold at the kept unit's own rate, or the member-mean rate); (d) random-partner groups with the OR gate; (e) R1 groups with the OR gate. Each pair differs by one part.
Name the vote rule 'R1 weighted by noise RMS'. Also report the pure-weight vote (rho = 1, no /sd) as a row, or justify the weighting with a 'Derived from:'.
Get t_M with a sort along dim 0 on the CPU (or kthvalue per column), not torch.quantile.
Hand the write to P4. When P4 is in, compute P4's fold with the merged firings, not a second write rule.
Scope round 2 to CLIP MLP or ResNet inner first, not both adapters in one build.
Add the 'Object (picked by)' column to the twin test and to the 3-child check.
verdicts.generic: Partly. Parents, the forest and the read sum carry to a language model. The OR gate needs a 'fires' threshold. GELU and ReLU have one at z > 0. SwiGLU does not, so the gate*up product needs its own adapter rule.

problems: The closed form is correct. The gradient condition M_KK W' S_KK = M_K: W S_:K gives W' = [I | A](W_K + W_C P). The reader weights g_r cancel from P, as the proposal says.

It still changes two things. P is the unit fold. A is a stream fold that writes cut stream dims onto kept dims. A does the same job as P6's per-site read maps L_l, from the writer side. Stacked with P6, it would count the fold twice.
Both planted tests recover exact copies: identical firings, identical M columns. They pass by algebra and test mechanics only. The evidence must come from the nulls.

The flat-output confound is strongest here. The ResNet 50% prediction of 6.2 is close to the estimated flat level of 5.7. The uncentred fold carries the mean message, and that alone can make the output less sure. That could give the whole predicted gain with no gain in agree.
The ResNet flat level (5.7) is an estimate. It is not measured.
The LN divisor is also a reader of the stream (P6's point). M ignores it. A adds energy to the kept dims, so the cut LN's sigma moves (risk 1). The proposal names this and gives a control.
The ln_pre fold covers only its bias. The gain part of the cut embedding dims is lost. This is minor.
The g_r from an isotropic probe on noise inherits F2.
The ResNet reader bookkeeping per stage (positions a, b, c) is easy to get wrong. Builder time is 1-1.5 h at best.
fixes: Add a switch for A. Always report an A = 0 row (unit fold only). That row is the part that combines with P6 later.
Keep both nulls (shuffled pairing, permuted A columns) and the M = I check. Call the planted tests 'implementation checks' in the log.

Measure the ResNet flat level with one line from the cached A logits. Then report agree next to each KL. A gain at 50% or 5% that lands near the flat level with no gain in agree is not a gain in kind.
Print sigma'/sigma at each LN for the floor and for the rule (one forward), as risk 1 says.
verdicts.generic: Yes. The adapter is a list of (writer matrix, firing tensor) and (reader rows, norm). It maps directly to SwiGLU down_proj, o_proj, RMSNorm and lm_head. S at d_ff x d_ff per layer can be built in chunks.

problems: Spec bug: vitgen.cut slices ln_pre to the kept dims (ln_pre = s(T['ln_pre'])). So the cut network's ln_pre is a LayerNorm over the kept dims only. The mask list names ln1, ln2 and ln_post, and leaves out ln_pre. With ln_pre unmasked, the masked forward does not equal the cut. The KL < 1e-5 check will fail.

T1 (pr_w = 0, so the gradient is 0) and T2 (a ReLU rescale, under which a*g does not change) pass by algebra. They show a known weakness of the floor. They do not show that the rule finds a real effect. Only T3 (the F1 loud dims in the top 5%) is a real known-answer test.

The read-permuted null scores W_u * R_pi(u), a product of norms. The rule scores (sum_t a*g)^2. So the null changes the form of the score AND breaks the pairing. A loss to this null does not show which of the two did it.
One probe per image over 128 images gives a noisy estimate of E_r[G^2] for low-score MLP neurons. The proposal plans seed 2 for the spread.
F2: Taylor scores on pink noise use gate states off the operating point. The white-noise control and P0 address this.

The predictions are optimistic but possible: ResNet 95% at .90 beats photo Minitron 1.113, and CLIP 95% is .55. The 50% predictions (7.5, 7.8) agree with thread 1: ranking alone cannot carry a cut job.
fixes: Mask the ln_pre input too: masked LN, with the output multiplied by m. Then the cut dims start at 0 in the stream and only collect writes that nothing reads.

Change the null: keep the same formula G[n,u] = sum_t a[n,u,t] * g[n,pi(u),t], with pi a permutation inside each set (shapes match inside a set). Keep the product-of-norms row as a second, labelled row if wanted.
Label T1 and T2 as implementation checks. T3 is the planted test that can fail.
Report agree and the flat level next to each KL.
Save the per-part KL at each greedy step, as a free 50% split readout (stream, heads, MLP).
verdicts.generic: Yes. Mask points are head outputs, SwiGLU products and stream dims at each RMSNorm input. The masked RMSNorm reaches the massive-activation dims through the divisor, the same effect as F1. The output probe is a centred Gaussian on the vocabulary logits.

problems: The rotation planted test passes by construction. Every step is coordinate-free, so the rule must give the same KL on the rotated teacher. critic.notes:
Cross-cutting checks for every proposal:

1. Flat-output confound. The floor at 50% sits near 9 on both networks. That is ABOVE the flat-output level: CLIP 6.28 (measured, in P4's text) and ResNet about 5.7 (an estimate). So the floor is confidently wrong. A rule that only makes the output less sure gains up to about 3 KL for free. The board shows the same sign at ResNet 5%: magcut (7.49) beats the floor (15.245). Rule for all builds: report agree (and top-1) next to every KL, and print the flat level on the board. A gain at 50% or 5% that lands near the flat level with no gain in agree is a calibration change, not a recovered job. P4's ResNet 50% prediction (6.2) and P1-P3's mean-only control are the most exposed.

2. Missing split. P1-P3, P4 and P6 each predict against an unmeasured 50% split by part (stream, heads, MLP). Measure it first (build step 0). It is cheap and decides which part can move the 50% number at all.

3. No tuning on check_bn. check_bn compares with stored BatchNorm statistics. A knob chosen by check_bn uses those statistics as data. Tune only on the held-split KL.

4. Planted tests that pass by algebra. In P1-P3 (twins), P4 (exact copies), P5 (T1, T2) and P6 (rotation), the planted object is recovered exactly by construction. They are good implementation checks. They do not show that the tool sees a real effect. In each case the named null carries the evidence, so the nulls must run in round 1, not later. The tests that can really fail: P0's photo-mix calibration, P5's T3, and the unread-direction test proposed for P6.

5. Network information only: all five pass. None uses photos, text or per-photo fits in the calculation. BatchNorm enters only as the folded inference map. P6 edits running_mean as a fold target, which is allowed. P0's generator runs the eval network, whose BN uses stored statistics as its own map, and no loss term targets them. The only rule stretch is P1-P3's vote, which adds noise RMS to R1 'in weights'.

6. Time: P0, P4 and P5 fit in about 1-1.5 h each. P6 needs about 1.5-2 h. P1-P3 needs well over 2 h. All calculations run in under 2 min on the Mac, one torch job at a time.

7. Predictions are sane. Every proposal says the 50% rows stay far from .856 / 1.801 with one part changed. That agrees with F3 and thread 1. The most optimistic: P5 at ResNet 95% (.90, better than photo Minitron 1.113), P4 at ResNet 50% (6.2, see point 1), and P1-P3 at ResNet 50% (7.0, better than photo Minitron 8.408 from noise only).
